clerk.hours: Monday through Friday, 8:30 a.m. to 4:00 p.m. Closed 12:00 to 12:30 for lunch.

records.title: Water and sewer rates for 2023
records.body: Council set the inside-village water rate at $6.40 per 1,000 gallons and the sewer rate at $8.15 per 1,000 gallons, effective April 1, 2023. Outside-village accounts pay one and one-half times those figures. Bills go out on the first of each month and are due the 20th. A 10 percent penalty applies after the due date. The clerk keeps the rate sheet at the window.

records.title: Parking on Market Street between Main and Lincoln
records.body: No parking on the east side of Market Street between Main Street and Lincoln Avenue from 7:00 a.m. to 9:00 a.m. on school days. The restriction does not apply on Saturday, Sunday, or days the Minerva Local Schools are closed. Signs go up at both ends of the block. The police department may ticket after a written warning for a first offense.

records.title: Regular Council meeting
records.body: Mayor Ruth Ellen Boyd called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. in council chambers. All members present. Minutes of October 17 were approved. The street superintendent reported two potholes on W Line Street were filled last Thursday. Ordinance 2023-11 on Market Street parking had a second reading and passed 5-0. Public comment: Tom Hale of 48 Lincoln Avenue asked when the leaf pickup would start. The mayor said the first pass is the week of November 27 if the weather holds.

records.title: Dog license fee and late penalty
records.body: A dog license for a village resident is $14 if paid by January 31. After January 31 the fee is $21. Kennel licenses stay at $60. The clerk sells licenses at the window. Bring proof of rabies vaccination. Tags are not mailed. This replaces the 2019 fee schedule. The county auditor still handles kennel inspections.

records.title: Certified copy fees at the clerk window
records.body: A plain copy is 10 cents a page. A certified copy of an ordinance, resolution, or set of minutes is $2.00 for the first page and 10 cents for each page after. Birth and death records are not sold here. Those stay with the health district. Cash only at the window. The clerk does not take cards.

records.title: Regular Council meeting
records.body: Mayor Boyd called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. Minutes of April 16 were approved as presented. Ordinance 2024-06 on copy fees had a third reading and passed 5-0. The finance committee asked the clerk to keep a paper log of certified copies sold. Public comment: none. Council adjourned at 7:41 p.m.

records.title: Sidewalk repair on Lincoln Avenue
records.body: Property owners on Lincoln Avenue between Market Street and High Street shall repair or replace broken sidewalk in front of their lots by October 31, 2024. The street department will mark slabs that trip. If an owner does not finish by that date, the village may do the work and assess the cost on the tax duplicate. Corner lots include both frontages. Driveway aprons are not part of this ordinance.

records.title: Regular Council meeting
records.body: Mayor Boyd called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. All members present except Councilmember Price, excused. Ordinance 2024-09 on Lincoln Avenue sidewalks passed 4-0. The clerk read a letter from the library board asking to use the parking lot on October 5 for the used book sale. Council agreed. No public comment. Adjourned 7:28 p.m.

records.title: Transient lodging tax of three percent
records.body: A three percent tax applies to rent for lodging of less than thirty days inside the village. The operator collects the tax and remits it to the clerk by the 15th of the following month. A bed-and-breakfast with two rooms or fewer is exempt. The clerk will print the return form. This tax does not apply to a stay paid by a government voucher.

records.title: Regular Council meeting
records.body: Mayor Boyd called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. Minutes of February 18 approved. Ordinance 2025-03 on lodging tax had a third reading and passed 5-0. The fire chief asked council to advertise for a part-time driver. Public comment: Jan Reese of 9 High Street said the stop sign at High and Market is faded. Street superintendent will order a new one. Adjourned 8:02 p.m.

records.title: Open burning in the village limits
records.body: Open burning of leaves, brush, or household trash is not allowed inside the village. A recreational fire in a metal ring or masonry pit, no larger than three feet across, is allowed if it is at least 25 feet from a structure. The fire department may order a fire out if smoke bothers a neighbor. This does not change the county burn ban when one is posted.

records.title: Regular Council meeting
records.body: Mayor Boyd called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. Minutes of August 19 approved. The clerk reported 41 dog licenses sold since January. Council set Halloween hours at 5:30 p.m. to 7:30 p.m. on October 31. Public comment: none. Adjourned 7:19 p.m.

records.title: Council meeting night and posting place
records.body: Council meets on the third Tuesday of each month at 7:00 p.m. in chambers at 12 W Line Street. If that Tuesday is a holiday, the meeting moves to the next business day. The posting place for ordinances and meeting notices is the glass case in the lobby and the bulletin board outside the clerk window. This replaces Ordinance 2016-12.

records.title: Organizational meeting
records.body: Mayor Boyd called the organizational meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. Council elected Carol Witt president pro tempore. Committee assignments stay the same as 2025. Ordinance 2026-01 on meeting night passed 5-0. The clerk swore in the new member from Ward 2, Daniel Cho. Public comment: none. Adjourned 7:33 p.m.

records.title: Regular Council meeting
records.body: Mayor Boyd called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. Minutes of May 19 approved. Street superintendent said the pothole on Market near the post office will be patched Thursday if the plant has mix. Council accepted a $500 donation from the Lions Club for the park fountain. Public comment: a resident asked about a dog park. The mayor said it is not on this year's budget. Adjourned 7:47 p.m.

records.title: Leaf pickup weeks for fall 2026
records.body: The street department will pick up loose leaves at the curb during the weeks of November 2, November 16, and December 7, 2026. Pile leaves at the curb, not in the street. No bags. No branches in the pile. If a truck cannot pass because of parked cars, that block waits until the next listed week. This ordinance expires December 31, 2026.

records.title: Regular Council meeting
records.body: Mayor Boyd called the meeting to order at 7:00 p.m. All members present. Minutes of July 21 approved. Ordinance 2026-05 on leaf pickup passed 5-0. The clerk noted that certified copies of the 2024 sidewalk ordinance are still selling. Public comment: none. Adjourned 7:22 p.m.
